# Churchill Downs Update: Kerness K, Concrete Glory Meet to Open Saturday's $1.2 Million Claiming Crown


## Nov 13, 2026


The 28th Claiming Crown drew 113 entries for its return to Churchill Downs on Saturday when some of North America’s top blue-collar Thoroughbreds will compete in nine supercharged starter allowances worth a combined $1.2 million.


First post is 1 p.m. (all times Eastern) for the 12-race card, which includes the $300,000 Dream Supreme (Listed) in Race 3 at 1:58 p.m. The Claiming Crown begins with the $100,000 Ready’s Rocket Express in Race 4 at 2:28 p.m. and concludes with the $175,000 Emerald at 6:23 p.m.


Churchill Downs will host the series for the fourth time in five years. The Claiming Crown, launched in 1999 by the National Horsemen’s Benevolent and Protective Association and the Thoroughbred Owners and Breeders Association, gives horses that have competed for a claiming price a chance to run for larger purses. This year’s program expands to nine races with the addition of the Empress, a six-furlong sprint for fillies and mares.


Here’s a look at all nine Claiming Crown races:


RACE 4 (2:28 p.m.): $100,000 READY’S ROCKET EXPRESS – Kerness K will seek his 12th straight victory when he faces two-time defending winner Concrete Glory as the 3-1 morning line favorite in the six-furlong Ready’s Rocket Express, which goes as Race 4 at 2:28 p.m.


Trainer Jamie Ness claimed Kerness K back for $7,500 in March. The gelding hasn’t lost since and leads North American Thoroughbreds with 11 wins this year. He rallied from fifth to win the Colonial Downs qualifier by a nose in August and extended his streak in a Maryland Million starter handicap at Laurel Park.


“I’m ready, he’s ready,” Chaun said in an interview Thursday at Parx. “Jamie told me he’s doing really good. I worked him last weekend. It’s a tough race but we’re ready.”


Concrete Glory can become the first horse to win three Claiming Crown races. The Saffie Joseph Jr. trainee is 10-1 on the morning line and will be ridden by 17-year-old apprentice Yomar Ortiz Jr.

RACE 6 (3:26 p.m.): $100,000 GLASS SLIPPER – TEC Racing’s Coquito will try to turn the tables on Argan as the 8-5 morning line favorite in the one-mile Glass Slipper, which goes as Race 6 at 3:26 p.m. The Joe Sharp trainee stalked the pace and took over on the turn to win a one-mile Claiming Crown qualifier on Aug. 22 at Colonial by 3 ½ lengths.


One month later, Argan went gate-to-wire in a starter allowance event at Churchill Downs to defeat Coquito by a half-length. Luis Saez rides Coquito while Walter Rodriguez has the mount on Argan.


Little Martha brings a five-race winning streak from Presque Isle Downs into her Churchill Downs debut. The Tamara Housel trainee drew post 10 and will be ridden by Mario Gutierrez.

RACE 7 (3:55 p.m.): $100,000 IRON HORSE KENT STIRLING MEMORIAL – JKX Racing’s Cowboy Mike, who won his first start for trainer Ernesto Padilla-Preciado by 8 ½ lengths Oct. 21 at Parx, is the 3-1 morning-line favorite for the 1 1/16-mile Iron Horse Kent Stirling Memorial, which goes as Race 7 at 3:55 p.m. The gelding was claimed for $8,000 out of a win at Del Mar in August. Ruben Silvera, who rode him at Parx, has the mount.


Freedom Road has finished second by a neck in each of the past two runnings of this race. The Richard Sillaman trainee held off fellow entrant Bill of Rights in an Aug. 22 Claiming Crown qualifier at Colonial and will be ridden Saturday by Jose Ortiz.

RACE 8 (4:25 p.m.): $100,000 EMPRESS – James Nelson’s Talkin in Cursive has won three straight for trainer Matt Shirer and is the 5-2 morning-line favorite for the six-furlong Empress, which goes as Race 8 at 4:25 p.m. The mare won at Ellis Park, Churchill Downs and Keeneland during her streak and will be ridden Saturday by Jaime Torres.


“It took us a little bit to figure out how to train her,” Shirer said. “She’s a little bit difficult at times but I think we’ve started to figure her out and she’s rewarded us since.”


Rocket Wrench Racing’s Miracle Ball has led at every call in each of her six straight wins at Canterbury Park and Prairie Meadows. Trainer Ruben Fuentes, a former Grade I-winning jockey in Southern California, said he won races as a jockey for Miracle Ball’s owners and they were the first to support his move to training horses.


“I’ve never had a horse win six in a row at any level, and I think at any level it’s pretty tough,” Fuentes told the National HBPA. “I think she’s got a big heart and she’s here to give a good race.”

RACE 9 (4:55 p.m.): $150,000 CANTERBURY TOM METZEN MEMORIAL – Thiele Thoroughbreds’ Initialize, beaten a nose two weeks ago in an allowance contest at Churchill Downs, is the 7-2 morning-line favorite for the Canterbury Tom Metzen Memorial, a 5 ½-furlong turf sprint that goes as Race 9 at 4:55 p.m. The Lacey Gaudet trainee will be ridden by Jaime Torres.


Defending winner Shape Note returns for trainer Mike Maker and jockey Jose Ortiz. The gelding won a Claiming Crown qualifier at Colonial by 1 ¾ lengths under Jareth Loveberry and has won 14 of 30 starts. His victory in this race last year was Maker’s record 23rd in the Claiming Crown.

RACE 10 (5:25 p.m.): $125,000 RAPID TRANSIT – Buckhead Racing’s Five o’ Somewhere is the 4-1 morning-line favorite for the seven-furlong Rapid Transit, which goes as Race 10 at 5:25 p.m. Trainer Matt Shirer won a 25-way shake to claim the gelding for $25,000 last November.


Five o’ Somewhere won a starter allowance at Churchill Downs under Luis Saez in May and finished third Oct. 21 at Keeneland in his first start in nearly five months. Saez returns to the saddle Saturday.


Trainer Carlos Santamaria will make his Claiming Crown debut with Workman Ranch’s Global Sensation. He claimed the 7-year-old at Ellis Park with Churchill Downs in mind, where the gelding already had won four times. Global Sensation lost a shoe in the race he was claimed out of, Santamaria said. He won his first start for the barn at Churchill in September, then finished second to fellow entrant Military Road at Keeneland. Jaime Torres has the mount.


Nation, who won last year’s Rapid Transit by 6 ¼ lengths, also returns for this year’s edition as a 30-1 longshot.

RACE 11 (5:54 p.m.): $200,000 JEWEL – Expect the Best, a 1 ¾-length allowance winner Oct. 1 at Horseshoe Indianapolis, is the 3-1 morning-line favorite for the 1 1/8-mile Jewel, the richest of the nine Claiming Crown races. Rafael Bejarano returns aboard the Ron Moquett trainee, who has finished in the money in all eight starts this year.


Thiele Thoroughbreds’ Indy Charges On finished third in an Aug. 22 seven-furlong Claiming Crown qualifier at Colonial before stretching back out to win an Oct. 11 starter allowance at Keeneland under Jose Ortiz for trainer Lacey Gaudet.


Gaudet described Indy Charges On as a stall walker and travels with a companion goat.


The Jewel goes as Race 11 at 5:54 p.m.

RACE 12 (6:23 p.m.): $175,000 EMERALD – Klaravich Stables’ Unit Economics (GB), a winner in his last two starts at Saratoga and Belmont Park, is the 6-5 morning-line favorite for the Emerald, which closes the card as Race 12 at 6:23 p.m. The Chad Brown trainee won a starter allowance at Belmont on Oct. 17 at the Emerald distance of 1 1/16 miles on turf. Tyler Gaffalione has the mount.


Victor Carrasco reunites with Tommy Humphries, Glynn Puryear and BHB Racing’s Free Advice. The duo won on turf at Horseshoe Indianapolis in August and finished second over the Matt Winn Turf Course Sept. 19 before winning a $120,000 allowance moved to the dirt Oct. 11 at Keeneland.


“I’ve ridden him in his last four starts, and he’s improved each time,” Carrasco said. “He can handle any surface, and he’s proven that throughout his career.”
